scenes.title: April 1861 Bicêtre Bedside: Leborgne Answering '21 Years' With Crisp Left-Hand Finger Counts While Saying Only 'Tan, Tan'

layout.description: Sunlit high-key 1861 Paris hospital examination room with tall arched French windows, a crisp white-linened bedside chair, Paul Broca's silver pocket watch and leather clinical notebook on an oak side table, and a matte-white anatomical plaster model highlighting the left third frontal convolution.

positions.who: Paul Broca (mannequin in 1861 dark French physician frock coat, white cravat, and waistcoat)
positions.where: holding open his silver pocket watch and asking Leborgne how many years he has lived at Bicêtre

positions.who: Louis Victor Leborgne / 'Monsieur Tan' (mannequin in neat 1861 white linen hospital shirt and cardigan)
positions.where: nodding with bright, alert eyes, gesturing 'Tan, tan' vocally while crisply opening his left hand four consecutive times (20) plus 1 single finger (= 21 years!)

props.name: 1861 silver pocket watch & '4 × 5 + 1 = 21 Years' ledger note
props.period_detail: proves Leborgne's sharp arithmetic, time reading, and spoken-question comprehension
props.physical_behavior: refutes any confusion between speech loss and dementia

props.name: matte-white cerebral cast marking the Left 3rd Frontal Convolution
props.period_detail: pinpoints the exact asymmetric left-frontal locus presented on April 18, 1861
props.physical_behavior: marks the birth of cortical localization

actions.verb_sequence: asks Leborgne how many years he has spent at Bicêtre and shows his pocket watch -> Leborgne replies 'Tan, tan' with expressive pitch while flashing four crisp 5-finger counts plus 1 finger to answer '21' accurately

reactions.reaction: records intact intelligence + preserved tongue motility alongside selective loss of *articulate language*
expresses clear relief at being understood accurately

scenes.wardrobe: 1861 Parisian physician frock coat, waistcoat, white collar; clean white linen hospital shirt and wool shawl cardigan.
scenes.recognition_hook: His mouth could pronounce only one syllable — 'Tan' — yet five seconds with Paul Broca's pocket watch proved a sharp, fully awake mind lived inside.

key_visual.description: an 1861 Paris hospital room where a seated patient answers a frock-coated physician's pocket-watch question by crisply flashing finger counts ('21') beside a matte-white left-frontal brain model

scenes.title: 2007 Paris MRI: Scanning Leborgne's 146-Year-Old Preserved Brain
scenes.era: 2007, Paris / UC Davis neuroimaging suite (Dronkers et al.)

layout.description: Clean bright modern MRI control suite displaying crisp 3D slices of Leborgne's preserved 1861 specimen.

positions.where: pointing on the high-resolution monitor to the deep white-matter tract lesion (Superior Longitudinal Fasciculus) extending far deeper than surface Broca's area

props.name: high-res 3D MRI slice display of Leborgne's 1861 brain
props.period_detail: reveals deep insula + SLF/arcuate tract involvement without cutting the historic specimen

actions.verb_sequence: scrolls from the famous 1861 surface dent deeper into the white-matter speech highway

reactions.reaction: nod seeing a 146-year clinical mystery resolved

scenes.wardrobe: 2007 tailored blazer and white lab coats.
scenes.recognition_hook: Because Paul Broca refused to slice 'Tan's' brain in 1861, a 2007 MRI scanner revealed what hid underneath for 146 years.

scenes.title: 'We Speak With the Left Hemisphere!' (1865 Asymmetry Breakthrough)
scenes.era: 1865, Société d'Anthropologie de Paris lecture hall

layout.description: Sunlit 19th-century oak lecture table displaying eight left-hemisphere case diagrams vs zero right-hemisphere aphasia cases.

positions.where: presenting the 8-to-0 left-vs-right hemisphere chart to astonished Parisian anatomists

props.name: 8 Left vs 0 Right hemisphere case ledger
props.period_detail: overturns centuries of assuming symmetrical twin hemispheres

actions.verb_sequence: points across eight consecutive left-frontal lesion diagrams

reactions.reaction: realize human brain hemispheres specialize asymmetrically

scenes.recognition_hook: Eight speech-loss brains in a row, all damaged on the LEFT — shattering the myth that our two hemispheres are identical twins.

scenes.title: Singing Across the Detour: Melodic Intonation Rehabilitation

layout.description: Warm sunlit therapy table where a therapist taps a gentle two-note rhythm with a left-hemisphere stroke survivor.

positions.where: tapping left-hand rhythm and singing 'Good mor-ning!' smoothly together using intact right-hemisphere melody circuits when plain speech stalls

props.name: two-note melodic rhythm cards
props.period_detail: recruits intact right-hemisphere frontotemporal singing network
props.physical_behavior: clinical payoff of Broca's lateralization discovery

actions.verb_sequence: struggles speaking prose -> taps rhythm and sings the full three-word phrase clearly

scenes.recognition_hook: When the left hemisphere's speech bridge is damaged, tapping a melody can route real words across the intact right hemisphere!
